title: Signals & Systems
subject: Signals & Systems
description: Continuous- and discrete-time signals, LTI systems, Fourier/Laplace/z-transforms and sampling. Built for the KV *Signale und Systeme* at JKU, with an eye on biomedical signals (ECG, EEG, ultrasound).

resources.title: Oppenheim, Willsky, Nawab – Signals & Systems (2nd ed.)
3Blue1Brown – But what is the Fourier Transform?

nodes.title: Mathematical foundations
nodes.description: Refresher of the maths the whole course rests on. Skip what you already master.

nodes.title: Complex numbers & Euler's formula
nodes.description:
Cartesian vs. polar form, $e^{j\theta} = \cos\theta + j\sin\theta$, phasors and why engineers write $j$ instead of $i$.

$$\cos(\omega t) = \tfrac{1}{2}\left(e^{j\omega t} + e^{-j\omega t}\right)$$
objectives: Convert between $a + jb$ and $r e^{j\theta}$ fluently
Multiply and divide complex numbers in polar form
Explain why a real sinusoid is a sum of two counter-rotating phasors

nodes.title: Integrals, series & the geometric sum
nodes.description: Improper integrals, $\sum_{n=0}^{N-1} a^n = \frac{1-a^N}{1-a}$ and its infinite version for $|a|<1$. Needed constantly for DT transforms.
objectives: Evaluate $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-a|t|}\,dt$
Sum finite and infinite geometric series with complex ratio

nodes.title: Signals
nodes.description: Classification and the elementary building blocks every later chapter uses.

nodes.title: Signal classification
nodes.description: Continuous vs. discrete time, energy vs. power signals, periodicity and fundamental period, even/odd decomposition.
objectives: Decide whether $x[n] = \cos(\tfrac{3\pi}{7} n)$ is periodic and find $N$
Compute energy and average power of a given signal

nodes.title: Elementary signals: δ, u, exponentials
nodes.description: The unit impulse $\delta(t)$ and its sifting property $\int x(\tau)\delta(\tau - t_0)\,d\tau = x(t_0)$, the unit step $u(t)$, real and complex exponentials, $\mathrm{rect}$ and $\mathrm{sinc}$.
objectives: State and use the sifting property
Sketch time-shifted and time-scaled versions of elementary signals

nodes.title: LTI systems
nodes.description: Linear time-invariant systems and the convolution integral/sum.

nodes.title: System properties
nodes.description: Linearity, time-invariance, causality, memory, BIBO stability, invertibility — and how to prove or disprove each.
objectives: Test an input–output relation for all five properties with a clean argument or counter-example

nodes.title: Impulse response & convolution
nodes.description:
Every LTI system is fully described by $h(t)$:

$$y(t) = (x * h)(t) = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x(\tau)\,h(t-\tau)\,d\tau$$

Graphical convolution (flip–shift–multiply–integrate), properties (commutative, associative, distributive), DT convolution sum.
objectives: Compute convolutions of piecewise signals graphically and analytically
Determine causality and stability from $h(t)$
Combine series/parallel LTI systems into one impulse response

prerequisites.note: DT convolution sums are geometric series

parts.label: a
hints: $h(t-\tau)$ is $h(\tau)$ flipped and shifted right by $t$.

parts.label: b
parts.solution: A trapezoid: linear ramps on $[-1.5,-0.5]$ and $[0.5,1.5]$, plateau of height 1 on $[-0.5,0.5]$, zero elsewhere.

exercises.title: Exponential through a step
exercises.statement: An LTI system has impulse response $h(t) = e^{-2t}u(t)$. Find the response to $x(t) = u(t) - u(t-1)$.
hints: Use linearity: respond to $u(t)$ first, then shift.
exercises.solution: $s(t) = \tfrac12(1-e^{-2t})u(t)$ is the step response, so $y(t) = s(t) - s(t-1)$.

nodes.title: Frequency-domain analysis
nodes.description: Representing signals as sums of complex exponentials — the eigenfunctions of LTI systems.

nodes.title: Fourier series
nodes.description: Periodic $x(t) = \sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty} a_k e^{jk\omega_0 t}$ with $a_k = \frac{1}{T}\int_T x(t)e^{-jk\omega_0 t}\,dt$. Parseval, Gibbs phenomenon, symmetry properties.
objectives: Compute $a_k$ of a square wave and sketch the line spectrum
Relate symmetry of $x(t)$ to properties of $a_k$

prerequisites.note: The eigenfunction property $e^{j\omega t} \mapsto H(j\omega)e^{j\omega t}$ motivates the whole chapter

nodes.title: Continuous-time Fourier transform
nodes.description: From series to transform as $T \to \infty$: $X(j\omega) = \int x(t)e^{-j\omega t}\,dt$. Properties (linearity, shift, modulation, convolution ↔ multiplication, duality), transform pairs, frequency response $H(j\omega)$ and ideal filters.
objectives: Derive the transform of $\mathrm{rect}$, $e^{-at}u(t)$ and $\delta(t)$
Use the convolution property to solve an LTI problem in the frequency domain
Sketch magnitude and phase of a first-order low-pass

flashcards.front: Convolution property of the Fourier transform

nodes.title: Sampling theorem & aliasing
nodes.description: Impulse-train sampling, spectrum replication at multiples of $\omega_s$, Nyquist rate $f_s > 2 f_{\max}$, ideal reconstruction and aliasing. Where it bites in practice: ECG at 250 Hz, ultrasound Doppler, MRI k-space.
objectives: Determine the minimum sampling rate for a band-limited signal
Predict the alias frequency of an undersampled sinusoid

exercises.title: Mains hum in an ECG
exercises.statement: An ECG amplifier picks up 50 Hz mains interference. The signal is sampled at $f_s = 80\,\text{Hz}$ without an anti-aliasing filter. At which frequency does the hum appear in the sampled signal?
hints: Aliases appear at $|f - k f_s|$ for integer $k$.
exercises.solution: $|50 - 80| = 30\,\text{Hz}$ — right inside the QRS band, which is why hardware anti-aliasing filters are mandatory.

nodes.title: Laplace transform & system functions
nodes.description: $X(s) = \int x(t)e^{-st}\,dt$, region of convergence, poles/zeros, $H(s)$ of differential-equation systems, stability from pole locations.
objectives: Find $H(s)$ and the ROC for a causal LTI system described by a differential equation
Decide stability from the pole-zero plot
